hook_text: Two bakkies: R189 950 and R198 590. Same six digits, but which one costs more?
clip_script: Two bakkies in Kimberley. R189 950 and R198 590. Split each price into two groups of three. One hundred and eighty-nine thousand, nine hundred and fifty. One hundred and ninety-eight thousand, five hundred and ninety. Now compare from the left. 1 and 1, the same. 8 against 9. Nine wins. R198 590 costs more, by R8 640. Same digits, different places, big difference. Now three game reserves: 245 318, 245 381 and 254 138 visitors. Smallest first: 245 318, then 245 381, then 254 138. Count the digits, start on the left, and move right only when the digits match.
visual_style: Two price tags split into a thousands group and a units group, then three visitor numbers sliding onto a number line.
mood: Curious, like a spot-the-difference game at a car dealer.
pacing: Read both prices, race the left-to-right comparison, then line up the three reserves.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and compare the prices of two things you would like to buy.
